listening.script:
Narrator: Part 3. You will hear some conversations between two or more people. You will be asked to answer three questions about what the speakers say in each conversation.
Narrator: Conversation 1.
Woman: Hi, I just received our office supply order, but the toner cartridges are missing.
Man: Let me check. I'm sorry, they were shipped separately from another warehouse. They should arrive tomorrow.
Woman: We really need them today. Our main printer is out of toner.
Man: In that case, I can have a courier bring them to you this afternoon at no charge.
Narrator: Conversation 2.
Man B: Hello, I'd like to schedule my annual check-up with Dr. Evans.
Woman B: Dr. Evans is on vacation until the twentieth. Would you like to see Dr. Patel instead?
Man B: I'd rather wait for Dr. Evans. She knows my medical history.
Woman B: Then the earliest appointment is on the twenty-second at nine thirty.
Man B: That's fine.
Narrator: Conversation 3.
Woman: Have you read the latest online reviews? Several customers said they waited too long for their food on weekends.
Man: That's because we only have two cooks on Saturday nights.
Man B: Hiring another cook would help, but it's expensive. What if we simplified the weekend menu? Fewer dishes would mean faster cooking.
Woman: Let's try that for a month and see whether the reviews improve.
Narrator: Conversation 4.
Man: Did you hear that the regional sales conference has been moved from May to June?
Woman B: I've already booked my flights.
Man: Oh no. Can you change them?
Woman B: I'll have to pay a fee, but the company should cover it. I'll check with accounting.
Narrator: Conversation 5.
Woman: Hi, I think I lost my credit card yesterday. I'd like to cancel it.
Man B: I can help you with that. Could you confirm your date of birth and the last four digits of the card?
Woman: Yes, it's March third, nineteen ninety, and the last four digits are four four one seven.
Man B: Thank you. The card has been canceled, and a new one will arrive within five business days. I don't see any unusual transactions on your account.
Narrator: Conversation 6.
Man: How are the preparations for the product launch going?
Woman: Good. The venue is booked, and the invitations have gone out. We're expecting about three hundred people.
Man: The room only holds two hundred and fifty.
Woman: Oh, I didn't realize. I'll call the venue and ask whether the larger hall is available.
Narrator: Conversation 7.
Woman B: Hi, I'd like two tickets for Saturday's jazz concert.
Man: I'm sorry, Saturday is sold out. We still have seats for Sunday afternoon.
Woman B: Sunday afternoon works. Are there any seats near the front?
Man: Yes, in row C. They're forty-five dollars each.
Woman B: Great, I'll take two.
Narrator: Conversation 8.
Man B: Hi, I'm Paul. It's my first day in the design department.
Woman: Welcome, Paul. I'm afraid your laptop isn't ready yet. The IT team is still installing the design software.
Man B: That's OK. Is there anything I can do in the meantime?
Woman: You could read through our brand guidelines. I'll print a copy for you. Your laptop should be ready by lunchtime.
Narrator: Conversation 9.
Woman: We've had several guests complain about the construction noise next door.
Man: The builders start at seven every morning. I asked them to start later, but they said they can't.
Woman C: Could we move the guests who are affected to rooms on the other side of the hotel?
Woman: Good idea. And let's offer them a free breakfast as an apology. Mei, can you check which rooms are available?
Narrator: Conversation 10.
Man: Could you prepare the sales charts for the board meeting using the new data software?
Woman B: I've never used that software before.
Man: Oh, Ken knows it well. I'll ask him to show you how it works this afternoon.
Woman B: Thanks. Then I'll have the charts ready by tomorrow morning.
Narrator: Conversation 11.
Woman: Hi, I'm moving to a new apartment next month, and I'd like an estimate.
Man B: Sure. How many bedrooms do you have?
Woman: Two. And there's a piano.
Man B: Pianos require special equipment, so there's an extra charge of one hundred and fifty dollars. I can send someone to look at your apartment on Thursday and give you an exact quote.
Woman: Thursday morning would be best.
Narrator: Conversation 12. Look at the shipping options.
Man: I'd like to send this package to Chicago, please.
Woman: Sure. When does it need to arrive?
Man: By Friday. Today's Wednesday, so it needs to get there in two days.
Woman: Express would arrive on Friday, but sometimes late in the day. If you need it by Friday morning, I'd choose next-day delivery.
Man: Let's do that, to be safe.
Narrator: Conversation 13. Look at the building directory.
Woman B: Excuse me, I'm looking for Brennan and Associates, the accounting firm.
Man B: They used to be in this building, but they moved to the building across the street last month.
Woman B: Oh, I see. They're still on the directory.
Man B: It hasn't been updated yet. Their new office is on the first floor, next to the bank.

listening.script:
Narrator: Part 4. You will hear some talks given by a single speaker. You will be asked to answer three questions about what the speaker says in each talk.
Narrator: Talk 1.
Woman B: Good afternoon, this is Claire from the Seaview Hotel, calling for Mr. Andrew Ross. I'm calling to confirm your reservation for a double room from June tenth to June thirteenth. You mentioned that you'd be arriving late, so could you let us know your expected arrival time? Our front desk is open twenty-four hours, but if you arrive after midnight, the main entrance will be locked, and you'll need to use the side door. Please call us back at five-five-five, zero one two three.
Narrator: Talk 2.
Man: Attention, all production staff. The new packaging machine on Line 3 will be installed this weekend. Starting Monday, it will replace the old machine completely. All workers on Line 3 must attend a training session before operating it. Sessions will be held on Monday and Tuesday at eight a.m. and two p.m. Please sign up with your supervisor by Friday. The training takes about two hours.
Narrator: Talk 3.
Woman C: This summer, discover the Riverside Zoo after dark! Every Friday evening in July and August, the zoo will stay open until ten p.m. for our Night Safari events. See which animals are most active at night, enjoy live music and grab dinner from our food trucks. Tickets are twenty dollars for adults and ten dollars for children, and zoo members get in free. Book online, as tickets for last year's events sold out quickly.
Narrator: Talk 4.
Man B: Welcome to the Old Town walking tour. Over the next two hours, we'll visit some of the city's oldest buildings, including the cathedral, the former merchants' hall and the market square. Most of the streets are made of cobblestones, and there are quite a few hills, so I hope you're wearing comfortable shoes. We'll stop for a coffee break at the halfway point. Please stay close to the group, as the streets can be very busy.
Narrator: Talk 5.
Woman: Let's look at the results of our customer satisfaction survey. Overall, satisfaction rose from seventy-eight to eighty-five percent this year. Customers were especially pleased with our faster delivery times. However, many said our Web site is difficult to navigate, particularly on mobile phones. So, improving the mobile site will be our top priority this quarter. I've asked the IT team to present a plan at our next meeting.
Narrator: Talk 6.
Man B: In travel news, SkyPath Airlines has announced that it will begin direct flights from Denver to Tokyo in April. The airline will operate four flights a week on the route, using its newest and most fuel-efficient aircraft. SkyPath says the flights are a response to growing demand from business travelers. To celebrate, the airline is offering discounted fares to passengers who book before the end of this month.
Narrator: Talk 7.
Woman C: Thank you for calling the Lyric Theater box office. Our box office is open from noon to eight p.m., Tuesday through Sunday. Tickets for all performances can also be purchased on our Web site. This season's opening show, The Winter Garden, begins on October fifth. Please note that latecomers will not be admitted until the intermission. For information about group discounts, press one. To speak with a staff member, please stay on the line.
Narrator: Talk 8.
Man: Good evening, everyone. We're here tonight to celebrate Margaret Hill, who is retiring after thirty-two years with the company. Margaret started as a receptionist and went on to become our director of operations. She opened our first overseas office in Singapore and trained many of the managers in this room, including me. Margaret, we'll miss your wisdom and your sense of humor. Now, I'd like to invite you to come up and accept a small gift from all of us.
Narrator: Talk 9. Look at the room schedule.
Woman: Hi, everyone. Just a quick update about tomorrow's customer service training. We'd planned to use the Oak Room, but the projector there isn't working. So we'll use the room next to the cafeteria instead, which seats up to thirty people. The training still starts at nine. Please bring your laptops, because we'll be practicing with the new customer database.
Narrator: Talk 10. Look at the chart.
Man B: Thanks for joining today's call. This chart shows our sales by region for the last quarter. As you can see, the West region had the highest sales, as usual. But I'd like to congratulate the team in the region with the lowest sales on the chart, because their sales grew faster than anyone else's, almost thirty percent compared with last year. Next quarter, we'll be adding two sales representatives to that team to support their growth.

Items left in the locker rooms are kept at the front desk for 30 days. After that, clothing is donated to a local charity, and other items are discarded. passages.title: Advertisement

SPEAK & MEET – Language Exchange Evenings
Want to practice a foreign language in a relaxed setting? Join us every Thursday from 7:00 to 9:00 P.M. at the Corner Café on Elm Street. Participants spend half the time speaking their own language and half the time speaking the language they are learning. Spanish, French, Japanese and English groups meet every week. LOCAL BAKERY WINS NATIONAL PRIZE
Rosewood Bakery, a small family business on Church Street, has won first prize in the National Bread Awards for its sourdough loaf. Owner Martin Fry, who opened the bakery with his wife in 2018, said they were "completely surprised" by the win. The bakery uses flour from a mill just ten kilometers away. Since the award was announced, demand has risen so much that the bakery now opens an hour earlier, at 6:00 A.M., and has hired two new bakers.

Survey: Workers Value Flexibility
A new survey of 2,000 office workers by Northgate Research has found that flexibility is now more important to employees than salary when choosing a job. Sixty-two percent of respondents said they would prefer a job with flexible hours over one that paid 10 percent more. The survey also found that workers who can work from home at least two days a week report higher job satisfaction. However, many respondents said they missed face-to-face contact with colleagues, and a third said they found it harder to learn new skills when working remotely. The researchers recommend that companies offer a mix of office and home working.

TWO TECH FIRMS TO MERGE
Brightwave Software and Coral Data announced yesterday that they will merge to form a new company, BrightCoral, by the end of the year. The combined company will have about 900 employees. Brightwave's CEO, Anita Rao, will lead the new company, while Coral Data's founder, Paul Kim, will become head of research. The companies say no jobs will be cut, but some teams will move to Brightwave's headquarters in Austin.

———

MEMO
To: Coral Data staff
From: Paul Kim
Re: Merger
As you may have read, we are joining Brightwave. Our research and customer support teams will remain here in Denver. The marketing team will relocate to Austin in January; the company will pay all moving costs. I will hold a meeting for all staff on Thursday at 4:00 P.M. to answer your questions.

———

To: Paul Kim
From: Jenna Ortiz
Date: September 18
Subject: Thursday meeting

Dear Paul,
I'm afraid I won't be able to attend Thursday's meeting because I'll be meeting a client in Chicago. As a member of the marketing team, I have some questions about the move. Could we speak by phone on Friday morning?
Jenna Ortiz
